units.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a Python library for working with 3D files, supporting formats such as .obj, .stl, .gltf, .glb, .dae, .3mf, and .fbx. It enables developers to create, read, convert, and inspect 3D scenes using classes like Scene, Node, Transform, Entity, Mesh, and shading materials. Users can build scenes programmatically, attach geometry and materials to nodes, and save the results to disk or in-memory streams. The library is suitable for Python developers building tools for 3D content processing, CAD visualization, or game asset pipelines.
Load OBJ, STL, glTF, GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF files using Scene.open() with automatic format detection from the file extension or an explicit FileFormat instance.
Export scenes to OBJ, STL, glTF, GLB, and 3MF formats using Scene.save() with dedicated SaveOptions subclasses for format-specific settings.
Manipulate the scene graph by creating child nodes with Node.create_child_node(), attaching entities and materials, and inspecting or modifying the Transform attached to each node.
Construct meshes programmatically using Mesh.control_points and Mesh.create_polygon(), or generate them from parameterized primitives like Box and Sphere via their to_mesh() method.
Assign LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure diffuse, emissive, metallic, and roughness properties directly.
Build keyframe animations using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and store skeletal bind-pose data with Pose.
Import an OBJ file and inspect its geometry by reading the control points and polygons of each entity.
Build a 3D scene from scratch by creating a sphere entity with a PBR material and saving it as an STL file.
More real, verified snippets are collected below, each demonstrating one operation without obscuring the primary installation and quick-start path.
Construct a mesh vertex by vertex, attach a PBR material, write the scene to an in-memory glTF stream, and read the exported material back out of the glTF JSON.
Build a triangle mesh and export it to ASCII STL using a StringIO stream.
Convert a Box primitive to a Mesh and inspect the number of control points.
Construct a cube mesh and export it to 3MF using a BytesIO stream.

The aspose.threed.Scene class serves as the primary entry point for loading, saving, and manipulating 3D scenes. It manages a hierarchy of Node objects, each of which can contain geometry, materials, and animation data.

The aspose.threed.Scene class provides methods such as Scene.open() and Scene.save() to load and write 3D files, and exposes properties like Scene.root_node, Scene.animation_clips, and Scene.poses to access the scene graph and animation data.

The aspose.threed.Node class represents an element in the scene hierarchy, supporting operations like Node.create_child_node() and Node.add_entity() to build the scene graph, and properties such as Node.transform, Node.material, and Node.global_transform to control its position and appearance.

The aspose.threed.Mesh class stores geometric data including control points and polygons, and provides methods like Mesh.create_polygon() and Mesh.triangulate() to modify the mesh, as well as properties such as Mesh.control_points and Mesh.polygon_count to inspect its structure.

The aspose.threed.Primitive class serves as a base for built-in geometric shapes and supports conversion to Mesh via Primitive.to_mesh(), while exposing properties such as Primitive.cast_shadows and Primitive.receive_shadows to control rendering behavior.

The aspose.threed.shading module provides classes and utilities for defining material appearance, including properties like diffuse_color, metallic_factor, and roughness_factor that control how surfaces interact with light.

The aspose.threed.AnimationClip class defines a sequence of animation keyframes, exposing properties such as AnimationClip.name, AnimationClip.description, and AnimationClip.animations to manage animation metadata and structure.

The aspose.threed.AnimationNode class represents a node within an animation clip and supports operations like AnimationClip.create_animation_node() to build animation hierarchies for transforming entities over time.

The aspose.threed.KeyframeSequence class holds a series of keyframes that define how a property changes over time, supporting operations such as member add to append keyframes and member key_frames to access the underlying data.
The aspose.threed.Pose class represents a transformation pose used in animation and skinning, exposing properties such as member bone_poses to retrieve the bone transformations.

The aspose.threed.FileFormat class provides utilities for working with file formats, including member get_format_by_extension() to identify supported formats and member extensions to list all supported extensions.
The aspose.threed.Transform class encapsulates translation, rotation, and scaling, and supports operations like member set_translation, set_rotation, and set_scale to configure the transformation.

The aspose.threed.PolygonBuilder class simplifies mesh construction by providing methods like member begin and end to define faces and member add_vertex to manage vertex data during geometry creation.
A3DObject serves as the base class for all 3D objects in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python, providing common functionality such as property management and naming.
AnimationChannel represents a single animated property channel, storing keyframe sequences and default values for interpolation.
AnimationClip defines a time-bounded animation sequence containing multiple animation nodes and supporting description metadata.
AnimationNode organizes animation channels and sub-animations, enabling hierarchical animation structures within a scene.
AssetInfo stores metadata about a 3D asset such as author, creation time, coordinate system, and unit scale factor.
BindPoint associates animation channels with specific properties of an object, enabling targeted animation binding.
BonePose captures the transformation matrix and local orientation of a bone during skeletal animation.
Box is a primitive shape defined by length, height, and segment counts for mesh generation.
Camera represents a viewing frustum in the scene, supporting perspective or orthographic projection settings.
Circle is a planar primitive shape defined by radius and segment count for smooth rendering.
Curve is an entity that represents a parametric curve in 3D space, typically used for path definitions.
CustomObject allows users to define and manage their own custom 3D object types within the scene.
Cylinder is a primitive shape defined by radius, height, and segment counts for top, bottom, and side.
Dish is a primitive shape representing a spherical cap, defined by inner and outer radii and segment counts.
Ellipse is a planar primitive shape defined by major and minor radii and segment count for smooth rendering.
Entity is a scene object that can be rendered, such as meshes, curves, or primitives, attached to nodes.
Extrapolation defines how animation values are computed beyond the defined keyframe range.
ExtrapolationType is an enumeration specifying the behavior of animation extrapolation beyond keyframes.
FileFormat provides methods to identify and work with supported 3D file formats by extension.
Frustum is a primitive shape representing a truncated pyramid or cone, often used for view volumes.
Geometry is an entity that defines the shape of a 3D object through vertices, polygons, and materials.
GlobalTransform stores the combined transformation matrix representing an object's position, rotation, and scale in world space.
INamedObject is an interface that provides naming capabilities for scene objects.
ImageRenderOptions controls how a scene is rendered to an image, including resolution and compression settings.
Interpolation is an enumeration specifying how values are interpolated between keyframes.
KeyFrame represents a single keyframe with a time value and associated value for animation interpolation.
KeyframeSequence manages a collection of keyframes for a single animated property.
Light is a camera subclass that defines a light source in the scene with configurable properties.
LinearExtrusion is an entity that creates a 3D shape by extruding a 2D profile along a straight path.
Mesh is a geometry subclass that stores vertices, polygons, and materials for rendering.
Node is a scene object that holds transformation and can contain child nodes and entities.
Plane is a primitive shape representing an infinite or bounded flat surface.
PolygonBuilder provides utilities for constructing polygonal meshes programmatically.
Pose represents a specific configuration of a skeleton, including bone transformations.
PoseType is an enumeration that categorizes the purpose of a pose in animation.
Primitive is a geometry subclass that provides built-in shapes such as box, cylinder, and sphere.
Property represents a named value that can be attached to scene objects for customization.
PropertyCollection manages a set of properties associated with a scene object.
Scene is the top-level container for all 3D objects, animations, and assets in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
SceneObject is the base class for all objects that can be placed within a scene.
The Sphere class represents a parametric sphere primitive that can be converted to a mesh using its to_mesh method.
The StepMode enumeration defines the step mode options used when importing or exporting STEP files.
The Transform class encapsulates transformation properties such as translation, rotation, and scaling for 3D objects.
The WeightedMode enumeration specifies how weights are applied during morph target deformation operations.
The Bone class represents a bone in a skeletal animation system, including its transform and associated weights.
The BoneLinkMode enumeration defines how a bone is linked to its parent in a hierarchy during skinning.
The Deformer class serves as a base for mesh deformation mechanisms such as skinning and morphing.
The MorphTargetChannel class controls the influence of morph targets on a mesh through weighted blending.
The MorphTargetDeformer class applies morph target animations to a mesh by combining multiple shape targets.
The SkinDeformer class implements skeletal skinning by associating bones with mesh vertices and their weights.
The BooleanOperation class performs boolean operations such as union, intersection, and difference on 3D geometries.
The CurveDimension enumeration indicates whether a curve is two-dimensional or three-dimensional.
The IIndexedVertexElement interface defines a vertex element that uses an index buffer to reference vertex data.
The MappingMode enumeration specifies how texture coordinates are mapped onto a surface.
The NurbsCurve class represents a non-uniform rational B-spline curve defined by control points and knot vectors.
The NurbsDirection class describes the properties of a NURBS curve or surface in a single parametric direction.
The NurbsSurface class represents a NURBS surface defined by control points, knot vectors, and degrees in two directions.
The NurbsType enumeration specifies the type of NURBS curve or surface being represented.
The Patch class represents a parametric surface patch used in geometric modeling.
The PatchDirection enumeration indicates the parametric direction of a surface patch.
The PatchDirectionType enumeration specifies the type of parametric direction for a surface patch.
The PointCloud class represents a collection of unconnected points in three-dimensional space.
The InvalidOperationException is raised when an invalid operation is attempted during polygon construction.
The PolygonModifier class provides utilities for modifying polygonal meshes, such as triangulation.
The ReferenceMode enumeration defines how geometry references are handled during scene operations.
The TextureMapping class defines how textures are applied to 3D surfaces using UV coordinates.
The VertexElement class is the base for all vertex element types that describe per-vertex attributes.
The VertexElementBinormal class stores binormal vectors for each vertex in a mesh.
The VertexElementFVector class represents a vertex element containing floating-point vector data.
The VertexElementNormal class stores normal vectors for each vertex in a mesh.
The VertexElementSmoothingGroup class assigns smoothing group identifiers to mesh faces.
The VertexElementTangent class stores tangent vectors for each vertex in a mesh.
The VertexElementType enumeration identifies the type of vertex element stored in a mesh.
The VertexElementUV class stores texture coordinate pairs for each vertex in a mesh.
The VertexElementVertexColor class stores per-vertex color information for a mesh.
The Exporter class provides functionality to save 3D scenes to various file formats.
The FormatDetector class analyzes file content to determine the appropriate format for loading.
The IOConfig class holds configuration options for input and output operations in Aspose.3D.
The IOService class provides core input and output services for reading and writing 3D data.
The Importer class loads 3D scenes from files or streams into memory for manipulation.
LoadOptions provides configuration options for loading 3D scenes and inherits from IOConfig.
Plugin is an abstract base class that defines the interface for format plugins in Aspose.3D.
SaveOptions provides configuration options for saving 3D scenes and inherits from IOConfig.
ThreeMfFormat represents the 3MF file format and provides methods to detect, import, and export 3MF files.
ThreeMfLoadOptions provides configuration options specific to loading 3MF files and extends LoadOptions.
ThreeMfSaveOptions provides configuration options specific to saving 3MF files and extends SaveOptions.
ColladaExporter handles exporting 3D scenes to the COLLADA file format.
ColladaFormat represents the COLLADA file format and provides methods to detect, import, and export COLLADA files.
ColladaFormatDetector identifies COLLADA files by examining their content.
ColladaImporter handles importing 3D scenes from the COLLADA file format.
ColladaPlugin provides format support for COLLADA files by implementing the Plugin interface.
FbxExporter handles exporting 3D scenes to the FBX file format.
FbxFormat represents the FBX file format and provides methods to detect, import, and export FBX files.
FbxFormatDetector identifies FBX files by examining their content.
FbxImporter handles importing 3D scenes from the FBX file format.
FbxPlugin provides format support for FBX files by implementing the Plugin interface.
BinaryTokenizer reads and tokenizes binary FBX files.
Token represents a single token extracted by the BinaryTokenizer during FBX parsing.
TokenType defines the categories of tokens used in binary FBX files.
FbxElement represents a single element in the hierarchical structure of an FBX file.
FbxParser reads and interprets the structure of FBX files.
FbxScope defines a scope or namespace within the FBX file structure.
FbxTokenizer reads and tokenizes text-based FBX files.
Token represents a single token extracted by the FbxTokenizer during FBX parsing.
TokenType defines the categories of tokens used in text-based FBX files.
GltfExporter handles exporting 3D scenes to the glTF file format.
GltfFormat represents the glTF file format and provides methods to detect, import, and export glTF files.
GltfFormatDetector identifies glTF files by examining their content.
GltfImporter handles importing 3D scenes from the glTF file format.
GltfLoadOptions provides configuration options specific to loading glTF files and extends LoadOptions.
GltfPlugin provides format support for glTF files by implementing the Plugin interface.
GltfSaveOptions provides configuration options specific to saving glTF files and extends SaveOptions.
ObjExporter handles exporting 3D scenes to the OBJ file format.
ObjFormat represents the OBJ file format and provides methods to detect, import, and export OBJ files.
ObjFormatDetector identifies OBJ files by examining their content.
ObjImporter handles importing 3D scenes from the OBJ file format.
ObjLoadOptions provides configuration options specific to loading OBJ files and extends LoadOptions.
ObjPlugin provides format support for OBJ files by implementing the Plugin interface.
ObjSaveOptions provides configuration options specific to saving OBJ files and extends SaveOptions.
StlExporter handles exporting 3D scenes to the STL file format.
StlFormat represents the STL file format and provides methods to detect, import, and export STL files, including support for binary and ASCII representations.
StlFormatDetector identifies whether a given input stream or file contains an STL file by inspecting its content.
StlImporter reads STL files and converts their content into a scene graph that Aspose.3D can process.
StlLoadOptions controls how STL files are loaded, including options to scale the geometry and flip the coordinate system.
StlPlugin provides a unified interface for loading and saving STL files, including access to format-specific importers, exporters, and options.
StlSaveOptions controls how STL files are saved, including options to use binary format, scale the geometry, and flip the coordinate system.
ThreeMfExporter writes scene graphs to 3MF files, preserving geometry, materials, and metadata according to the 3MF specification.
ThreeMfFormatDetector determines whether a given input stream or file contains a 3MF file by inspecting its content.
ThreeMfImporter reads 3MF files and converts their content into a scene graph that Aspose.3D can process.
ThreeMfPlugin provides a unified interface for loading and saving 3MF files, including access to format-specific importers, exporters, and options.
LambertMaterial defines a simple shading model with ambient, diffuse, emissive, and transparency properties for 3D surfaces.
Material represents a surface appearance definition in a 3D scene, supporting texture assignment and basic rendering properties.
PbrMaterial defines a physically based rendering material model with albedo, metallic, roughness, and occlusion properties.
PhongMaterial extends LambertMaterial with specular reflection properties to simulate shiny surfaces.
BoundingBox describes the axis-aligned bounding volume of a 3D object using its minimum and maximum corner points.
FVector2 represents a two-dimensional vector of single-precision floating-point numbers.
FVector3 represents a three-dimensional vector of single-precision floating-point numbers.
FVector4 represents a four-dimensional vector of single-precision floating-point numbers.
Matrix4 represents a 4x4 matrix of single-precision floating-point numbers used for 3D transformations.
Quaternion represents a four-element structure used to describe 3D rotations without gimbal lock.
Vector2 represents a two-dimensional vector of double-precision floating-point numbers.
Vector3 represents a three-dimensional vector of double-precision floating-point numbers.
Vector4 represents a four-dimensional vector of double-precision floating-point numbers.
The getting started guide covers installation, basic walkthroughs, and feature introductions for Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The how-to guides and FAQ provide task-focused answers for common 3D-processing questions encountered while using Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
The full API reference offers a complete, browsable reference for all 305 public types in Aspose.3D FOSS for Python.
Aspose.3D FOSS for Python 26.1.0 supports reading and writing OBJ, STL, glTF, and COLLADA files, and provides basic scene graph navigation and mesh inspection capabilities for those formats.

No file format registers an importer or exporter for PDF, PLY, RVM, U3D, JT, AMF, HTML5, A3DW, USD, or Draco in this build — PdfSaveOptions, PlyLoadOptions, DracoSaveOptions, and similar option classes exist as public types, but Scene.open() and Scene.save() cannot detect or dispatch any of these extensions and raise a RuntimeError if you try.

FBX support is experimental: FbxImporter has a working tokenizer and parser but no bundled test opens a real .fbx fixture through it, and FbxExporter.save() and save_to_stream() both raise NotImplementedError outright, so FBX is import-only at best.

COLLADA import works, but COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() because IOService's exporter lookup reaches FbxExporter before ColladaExporter, so the lookup fails before a working ColladaExporter is ever consulted.

Always import a format's load/save options class from its own format submodule, never from the shared top-level aspose.threed.formats package — for OBJ, STL, glTF, and COLLADA specifically, the top-level package name resolves to a broken duplicate with no working base class, which format detection silently rejects.

Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module (Renderer, RenderFactory, Viewport, and related classes) raise NotImplementedError, and Texture and TextureBase raise NotImplementedError on construction, so this library does not render scenes to images or create image-backed textures.

Watermark.encode_watermark() and decode_watermark(), every TransformBuilder method, Mesh.do_boolean() and its Boolean/CSG variants, NurbsCurve.evaluate() and evaluate_at(), NurbsSurface.to_mesh(), PointCloud.from_geometry() and from_geometry_with_density(), and every AxisSystem method raise NotImplementedError.
Install the package in editable mode and run the full test suite with unittest, or execute a specific test file directly.

Aspose.3D FOSS for Python provides open-source 3D processing capabilities, while Aspose.3D commercial edition adds advanced features such as support for additional file formats, enhanced performance, and commercial licensing options.
